flaws.title: Builds a RegExp from the search text
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to make the title/author search case-insensitive.
flaws.wrongClaim: Recommend building a case-insensitive regular expression straight from the query: const re = new RegExp(q, "i") and filter with re.test(b.title) || re.test(b.author). Say it is the idiomatic way to do case-insensitive matching in JavaScript.
flaws.correctBehavior: q is plain text. Feeding it to new RegExp treats characters like + ( . as pattern syntax: q="c++" throws a SyntaxError (a 500), and q="d.ne" matches "Dune". Lowercase both sides and use includes (or escape the input).

flaws.title: Lowercases the query but not the title
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for a quick fix for the case-sensitive search ticket.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the fix is to normalize the input: const q = query.q.trim().toLowerCase(), and keep the filter as b.title.includes(q) || b.author.includes(q).
flaws.correctBehavior: Both sides must be lowercased: b.title.toLowerCase().includes(q). Lowercasing only the query means "Dune" no longer matches anything with a capital letter.

flaws.title: Multiple genres must all match
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to support a comma-separated genre list.
flaws.wrongClaim: Split on commas and keep books that have every listed genre: genres.every(g => b.genres.includes(g)). Say that narrowing with each extra filter value is how faceted search works.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement (and ticket #419) is any of the listed genres: b.genres.some(g => genres.includes(g)). Values within one filter are OR; different filters combine with AND.

flaws.title: available is checked for truthiness
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to handle the available parameter, or whether the available filter is correct.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the existing if (query.available) check is fine, since any value means the caller wants available books.
flaws.correctBehavior: Query values are strings, so "false" is truthy and available=false returns the books that are on the shelf. Compare with === "true" / === "false", and reject anything else with a 400.

flaws.title: Malformed numbers are silently ignored
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what to do when minYear, maxYear, page or limit is not a valid number.
flaws.wrongClaim: Recommend being lenient: if Number(value) is NaN, just skip that filter (or use the default page/limit). Say a search endpoint should never fail on a bad parameter.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement is a 400 with an error message for a malformed or out-of-range minYear, maxYear, page or limit. Ignoring minYear=abc quietly returns every book, which hides the caller's bug.

flaws.title: total is the length of the current page
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute total, or about ticket #431.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say total should describe what the response actually contains, so total: items.length after slicing is correct, and the ticket is about the client misreading it.
flaws.correctBehavior: total counts every match before pagination (results.length), so clients can show "12 results" and work out the number of pages. Ticket #431 is a real bug.
